notes:
I couldn't do this research, so I have no notes to give you. My first search failed because of a mistake in my own code. Before I could fix it and search again, I hit the limit on tool use for this turn. As a result, I didn't read any pages from the approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages say and to give a URL for every point. Writing commentary from memory would break those rules, so I haven't written any.

If you ask again, I'll run the searches and read the pages. The plan:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word, Bible Hub and StudyLight (Gill, Ellicott, the Pulpit Commentary, Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*), and Precept Austin.
- **Protestant traditions:** Wesley's notes (wesley.nnu.edu), Ligonier / The Gospel Coalition / Desiring God, LCMS / 1517, and Sam Storms / AG. I'll only note a split where one really shows up. On this psalm, the most likely place is how the anointing oil and Aaron's priesthood (v. 2) are applied to Christ, the Spirit or church unity.
- **Other views:** NET Bible notes (for example, on "harmony," the oil on the "collar," and the geography of Hermon and Zion), Bible Odyssey, and Catholic/Orthodox sources such as Augustine on the Psalms at newadvent.org. I'll also look for debated popular teaching, such as "anointing" or "commanded blessing" sermons, if the sites discuss it.
